answer: Harberger identity seats: every agent holds its seat at a self-assessed price it pays a recurring tax on, and anyone may buy that seat at that price at any moment. A violet seat card stays always for sale. One treasury cannot fund ten clones, because each seat's price must exceed what the incumbent cohort loses by being diluted, and that figure grows with the cohort. The tax scales with the declared value, so a sybil farm's bill rises faster than its headcount, and a single shared ember of funding makes every seat instantly purchasable. Continuity is renewed each dawn, never owned.
